fact: The Ghana Statistical Service announced on 12 March 2026 data-sharing agreements with 25 ministries, departments and agencies to improve administrative data systems and statistical coordination, as reported by Ecofin Agency on 2026-09-22.

On 22 July 2026 the Ghana Statistical Service met the Education Ministry, Ghana Education Service and National Identification Authority on the Pilot Register-Based Education Statistics Project, and the Education Minister agreed to chair its steering committee.

The Ghana Statistical Service signed a memorandum of understanding with 25 ministries, departments and agencies, including the Births and Deaths Registry, Health Service and Police Service, to coordinate and share administrative data for official statistics; about 17 MDAs had draft data-sharing policies.

The Births and Deaths Registry published its 2022 Statistical Report: Death Registration, which presents statistics on deaths registered in 2022 drawn from all 261 districts; the preface calls it the inaugural statistical report by the Registry; as_of is the publication date 2024 (copyright 2024), the figures cover 2022.

The Births and Deaths Registry published its 2022 Statistical Report Birth Registration, with sections on birth registration process, data compilation and data source and figures on registered births in 2022 by region, sex, place of birth and mother's age; as_of is the publication date 2024 (copyright 2024), the figures cover 2022.

Statistics Denmark's terms of reference say the Ghana Statistical Service and Statistics Denmark signed an MoU for a 2024-2027 second phase and are contracting a consultant, for October-November 2024, to map digitised administrative data in Ghanaian MDAs for statistical use.
